states.basis: Chapter 18 'Construction Contractors and Home Inspectors' is the primary licensing chapter for plumbers in Alaska; plumbing contractors are classified as construction contractors under this chapter's registration and enforcement provisions.

None of the listed Kansas chapters contain plumbing contractor licensing. Chapter 65 (Public Health) covers various health professions and occupational therapies but does not include plumbing. Chapter 44 (Labor and Industries) is general labor law. Kansas does not appear to have state-level licensing for plumbers in the provided statute list; plumbing regulation is typically handled at the local/municipal level by individual cities and counties.

Plumbers and plumbing contractors are not listed in any of the provided Mississippi Title 73 (Professions and Occupations) chapters. While Mississippi has a Chapter 59 on Residential Builders and Remodelers and Chapter 60 on Home Inspectors, plumbing is not explicitly mentioned. The provided chapters cover specific licensed professions (architects, engineers, nurses, etc.) but do not include a dedicated plumbing licensing chapter, and no umbrella 'Contractors' or 'Construction Industries' chapter is shown in the list.

Plumbing contractors are typically licensed under state occupational/professional licensing frameworks; Chapter 71 (Public Health and Welfare) is the most likely container for such licensing in Nebraska's structure, though the specific plumbing licensing article is not individually listed and requires expansion to confirm.

Plumbers in New York are licensed under the General Construction Law (GCN), which contains Article 405 governing master plumbers and journeyman plumbers; this broad construction-trades container is not subdivided in the provided chapter list, so it is identified as the umbrella container to expand.

Plumbers are licensed in Pennsylvania under the Uniform Construction Code (UCC), which is referenced in Title 8 Chapter 32A and Title 11 Chapter 141A for municipalities, but the primary state-level licensing statute is not visible in this chapter list. The profession is regulated at the state level but requires access to the consolidated statutes or a broader occupational licensing code not explicitly listed here.

Plumbers are typically licensed under a broad 'Contractors' or 'Construction Industries' licensing chapter in Tennessee Code Title 62, which is not fully enumerated in the provided list. The profession is clearly state-regulated but the specific chapter containing plumbing contractor licensing is not shown among the Title 63 health-related boards or the other chapters listed.
Article 42, 'West Virginia Contractor Licensing Act,' is the specific chapter that licenses plumbers and plumbing contractors as a classification of contractors under state law.

Plumbers and plumbing contractors are not listed in Wyoming Title 33's specific licensing chapters. Chapter 42 covers water well drilling and pump installation contractors (a related but distinct trade), and Chapter 1 is general licensing administration. Wyoming does not appear to regulate plumbing at the state level in this statute list; plumbing licensing in Wyoming is typically handled at the local/municipal level.
